title: Two-stage Slowdown of Vacancy-mediated Diffusion in a Lattice Gas Model with Quenched Disorder and Spins
abstract: We present a lattice gas model with random interactions quenched in space and spins quenched to the particles. The vacancy-mediated diffusion is studied in equilibrium. A two-stage slowdown is witnessed in both the mean squared displacement and the spatial overlaps. We demonstrate that the plateaus are due to anti-correlation at the corresponding length scale. The anti-correlation diminishes quickly with increasing lag time. A broad and yet finite distribution of the survival function of vacancies suggests their normal diffusion at large time limit. Our model can serve as a new playground for understanding hierarchical dynamics in glassy-like dynamical systems.
summary: This work analyzes vacancy-mediated diffusion in a disordered lattice gas model, observing a characteristic two-stage slowdown in transport properties. This slowdown is linked to anti-correlations arising from sequential trapping and rare jumps within the disordered energy landscape. The findings provide a framework for understanding hierarchical dynamics in glassy systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the two-stage slowdown of vacancy-mediated diffusion in a lattice gas model subjected to quenched disorder and random spins.
main_result: The diffusion exhibits a two-stage slowdown characterized by plateaus in MSD and spatial overlap, attributed to anti-correlations at specific length scales, suggesting hierarchical dynamics.
method: The study uses Monte Carlo simulations with Metropolis dynamics to track particle and vacancy movement in the disordered lattice gas.
model_or_system: The system is a lattice gas model on a 2D square lattice with quenched random interactions ($J_{ij}$) and quenched spins ($s_{p_i}$). Particle hopping occurs when a nearest neighbor is a vacancy.
key_observables: Mean Squared Displacement (MSD), Spatial Overlap Function ($q(t)$), and Displacement Correlation Function ($C(k	au)$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (e.g., $T=0.22$), particle density ($ho=0.99$), and various time/length scales ($	au$, $k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system dynamics can be described by hopping rates derived from the Hamiltonian, and that the observed slowdown reflects underlying trapping mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures show the two-stage slowdown in MSD and spatial overlap for both particles and vacancies, and the correlation function $C(k	au)$ confirms anti-correlations at different time lags.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model and observables, presents evidence for the two-stage slowdown in MSD and $q(t)$, analyzes vacancy motion via trapping mechanisms (Type I and Type II), and concludes by discussing the implications for hierarchical dynamics.
why_interesting: The concept of hierarchical dynamics and slow relaxation in disordered systems is highly relevant to understanding glassy dynamics in many-body quantum systems, connecting classical lattice models to complex quantum relaxation phenomena.
